Historian Rebecca Lemov wrote a history of brainwashing research and now studies the sciences of mind control at Harvard. On Danny Jones's podcast, she explains why she fears MK-Ultra, the CIA's notorious mind control program, is still active in modern forms, carried on by new institutions with better tools.

Lemov's authority is archival; she has read the program's surviving records and interviewed its world. She connects the Cold War experiments to today's data-driven influence systems with a scholar's care for the differences. Jones draws out the continuities that alarm her. The episode offers the strongest historically grounded version of a popular fear, from the person best qualified to judge the original. Listeners can weigh her evidence for survival of the program's spirit against the official story of its burial.
podcast-tuckercarlson-DE2AVar-XNc:
Maine reporter Steve Robinson joins Tucker Carlson to expose a drug network in his state. Carlson calls him one of the last independent journalists in Maine. Their film on the case is called High Crimes.

Robinson says Chinese cartels took over drug trade in the rural Northeast. He blames ignored border laws and failed local duty. The title also charges that politicians cover the trade up. Carlson presents the story as proof of a wider takeover. Listeners get a local reporter's case that stunned even a veteran host. The film extends the same case on screen.
